Gate evidence (AC4: make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero).

All commands run in worktree /Users/joeoakhart/fix-304e-container-lock with the worktree venv
first on PATH (env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"), against the change that merged as
5ef138d26e815d9b583a48656e3cb50e8fb02ab9.

1. make lint -> exit 0.
   Tail: "No findings to report. Good job! (1 suppressed)" / actionlint (all workflows).
   (An earlier run failed E501 on tests/unit/test_lock_container_recreate.py:115; the line was
   wrapped and lint re-run clean.)

2. make typecheck -> exit 0.
   "mypy src/rebar ... Success: no issues found in 399 source files".

3. Default suite (make test = pytest -m "not integration and not external") -> 
   "8214 passed, 38 skipped, 131 deselected, 13 warnings" in 1784.25s.
   That run also reported 1 ERROR in tests/unit/test_code_review_public_exposure.py
   ("Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT"). That error was caused by MY OWN concurrent
   `rebar comment` / `rebar create` / `rebar link` writes into the same worktree while the
   suite was running — not by this change. Re-run in isolation immediately afterwards:
   `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_public_exposure.py -p no:randomly -q` -> "5 passed".
   The change touches only src/rebar/_store/lock.py and adds one new test file; it has no
   relationship to the code-review public-exposure test.

4. Independent confirmation of the same gates by CI: Gerrit change 1138 received
   **Verified +1** from the rebar CI bot (GitHub Actions run 30667153643), which runs
   build/test/lint/typecheck, and **LLM-Review +1** ([LLM-Review: PASS], 3 advisory
   non-blocking findings). Both gates green were the precondition for Submit; the change is
   MERGED as 5ef138d26e815d9b583a48656e3cb50e8fb02ab9 on main.

5. Post-merge re-verification: the worktree was reset --hard to the merged commit and
   `pytest tests/unit/test_lock_container_recreate.py tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`
   -> "31 passed", confirming the fix and its tests landed intact after Gerrit's server-side
   rebase.

Coverage of the other acceptance criteria:
- AC1 (same-host orphan reclaimable despite a changed container hostname):
  tests/unit/test_lock_container_recreate.py::test_container_recreate_orphan_is_reclaimed and
  ::test_dead_owner_in_same_namespace_is_reclaimed.
- AC2 (live process never reclaimed; foreign host not reclaimed on hostname alone):
  ::test_live_owner_in_same_namespace_is_still_never_reclaimed,
  ::test_foreign_host_is_still_never_reclaimed,
  ::test_cross_namespace_reclaim_requires_the_fcntl_proof, plus every pre-existing
  yaw-gravel-linen test in tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py still passing unchanged.
- AC3 (an unprovable lock does not block indefinitely): the incident class is now provable, so
  it does not block at all — end-to-end replication through the real entry point (rebar.comment
  past an orphan left by a recreated container) completes in 0.18s versus the incident's ~62s
  then failure. No age ceiling was added, deliberately: reclaiming an unprovable foreign-host
  lock on a timer is exactly the loosening yaw-gravel-linen forbids. run_ensures already
  surfaces a LockTimeout as a WARNING rather than swallowing it silently; the remaining
  boot-path budget concern is filed as e43f-0d14-13f9-408f (arrogant-mesodermal-flyingfox),
  linked discovered_from this ticket.
